t.6.7.1: Thus addressed by the lord of the Rākṣasas, those mighty Rākṣasas all spoke with joined palms to Rāvaṇa, the sovereign of the Rākṣasas.
t.6.7.2: O king, our army is exceedingly great, thronged with iron clubs, spears, swords, tridents and battle-axes; why then do you give yourself over to despair?
t.6.7.3: Dhanada, who dwells on the peak of Kailāsa surrounded by many Yakṣas, was made subject to you after you had wrought a very great slaughter.
t.6.7.4: O lord, that mighty guardian of the world, who prided himself on his friendship with Maheśvara, was conquered by you in battle out of wrath.
t.6.7.5: Having slain the hosts of Yakṣas, having thrown them into turmoil and having fought them, you carried off this aerial chariot from the summit of Kailāsa.
t.6.7.6: O bull among Rākṣasas, Maya, the lord of the Dānavas, desiring friendship with you out of fear of you, gave you his daughter to be your wife.
t.6.7.7: The lord of the Dānavas named Madhu, swollen with pride in his valour and hard to approach, who brings happiness to Kumbhīnasī, was fought and brought under your control.
t.6.7.8: O mighty-armed one, having gone to Rasātala, you conquered the Nāgas; Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Śaṅkha and Jaṭī were brought under your sway.
t.6.7.9: O lord, the Dānavas, imperishable, mighty and heroic, who had moreover obtained boons, fought with you in battle for a whole year.
t.6.7.10: Relying on your own strength, O tamer of foes, you brought them under your sway, and there, O lord of the rākṣasas, you acquired many magical powers.
t.6.7.11: O mighty-armed one, the sons of Varuṇa, heroic and powerful, followed by their fourfold army, were vanquished by you in battle.
t.6.7.13: A great victory was won and death was warded off, and by your excellent fighting there all the worlds were thoroughly gladdened.
t.6.7.12: O king, you plunged into the ocean of Yama's army, whose great crocodile was the rod of Death and which was adorned with the island of Śālmali.
t.6.7.14: The earth was filled with many heroic kṣatriyas whose valour equalled that of Śakra, as if with mighty trees.
t.6.7.15: In valour, virtue and energy Rāghava is no match in battle for those warriors; yet you, O king, forcibly slew them, though they were exceedingly hard to conquer.
t.6.7.16: O king, this calamity that has come upon us from a common man is unfitting; you should not take it to heart at all. You will slay Rāghava.
